units: <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:4:1">Cant. R. to II, 4</cite> <he>ודִגְלוֹ</he> Michael and his band (of angels); a. e.—Pl. <he>דְּגָלִים</he>.

Num. R. s. 2 והיו כולם עשויים ד׳ ד׳ וכ׳ and all of them (the angels) were arranged in divisions, as it is said (Cant. V, 10) dagul (surrounded by divisions) of a myriad each (with ref. to Ps. LXVIII, 18).
<cite ref="Psalms 68:18">Ib.</cite> <he>עֲשֵׂה אותם ד׳ וכ׳</he> divide them into cohorts as they desired (with ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 2:2">Num. II, 2</cite>); v.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:4">Cant. R. to II, 4</cite>; Tanḥ. B’midb. 10.—
Ex. R. s. 15 אין ד׳ אלא צבאות d’galim means hosts.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15:6">Ib.</cite> <he>דִּגְלֵי השמים … וד׳ הארץ וכ׳</he> the heavenly hosts are the angels, the earthly hosts (of the Lord) are Israel.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15:6">Ib.</cite> s. 24, end; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 5a">Sabb. 5ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 98a:2">98ᵃ</cite> <he>דומה לדִגְלֵי מדבר</he> resembling the marches of the Israelites in the desert.
